questions.stem: Which gases are exchanged in plant leaves?
questions.explanation: Plants exchange carbon dioxide (needed for photosynthesis) and oxygen (product of photosynthesis, needed for respiration) through the stomata in their leaves.

questions.stem: During the day, which gas do leaves mainly absorb?
questions.explanation: During the day, leaves mainly absorb carbon dioxide for photosynthesis. They also take in some oxygen for respiration, but the net exchange is CO2 in and O2 out.

questions.stem: At night, what happens to gas exchange in plants?

options.text: The plant takes in more carbon dioxide
Only respiration occurs, so the plant takes in oxygen and releases carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: At night, there is no light for photosynthesis, so only respiration occurs. The plant takes in oxygen and releases carbon dioxide, the opposite of what happens during the day.

questions.stem: How are air spaces in the spongy mesophyll important for gas exchange?

options.text: They allow gases to circulate freely and reach all cells by diffusion

questions.explanation: The large intercellular air spaces in the spongy mesophyll provide a network through which CO2 and O2 can diffuse freely, ensuring all cells have access to the gases they need.

questions.stem: What is the compensation point for a plant?

options.text: The temperature at which the plant dies
The point where all stomata are closed
The light intensity at which the rate of photosynthesis equals the rate of respiration

questions.explanation: The compensation point is the light intensity at which photosynthesis and respiration occur at equal rates, resulting in no net gas exchange - CO2 produced equals CO2 used.

questions.stem: How do stomata facilitate gas exchange?

options.text: They actively pump gases in and out
They provide pores through which CO2 diffuses in and O2 diffuses out

questions.explanation: Stomata are small pores that allow gases to diffuse in and out of the leaf. CO2 diffuses in for photosynthesis and O2 diffuses out as a waste product.

questions.stem: Why do plants still need to respire even though they photosynthesise?

options.text: They do not need to respire
Respiration releases energy from glucose for cellular processes; photosynthesis only makes glucose

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis produces glucose but does not release usable energy. Plants must respire (24 hours a day) to break down glucose and release the ATP energy needed for growth, active transport, and other cellular processes.
